record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Let α be a free, probability-measure-preserving, ergodic action of F_2 on a measure space (X, μ). Determine whether (i) for each nonidentity x in F_2 there is another free p.m.p. action β with the same orbit equivalence relation E_α = E_β and such that x acts ergodically in β, and (ii) there is a free p.m.p. action β with the same orbit relation in which every nontrivial element of F_2 acts ergodically.

evidence.quote: Problem 45. Let α be a free, probability measure preserving (p.m.p.) and ergodic action of F2 on measure space (X, µ). (i) If e ̸= x ∈ F2, is there a free, p.m.p action β such that Eα = Eβ and x acts ergodically? (ii) (Miller–Tserunyan). Is there a free, p.m.p action β such that every nontrivial element of F2 acts ergodically?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F_2$ denote the free group on two generators, and let $\alpha\colon F_2 \curvearrowright (X,\mu)$ be a free, probability-measure-preserving (p.m.p.), ergodic action on a standard probability space. Recall that an action is free if every nonidentity group element acts without fixed points (up to a null set), and an element $g \in F_2$ is said to act ergodically in an action $\beta$ if the transformation $\beta(g)\colon X \to X$ has only trivial invariant measurable sets (i.e., of measure $0$ or $1$). Two p.m.p. actions $\alpha,\beta$ of $F_2$ on $(X,\mu)$ have the same orbit equivalence relation if $E_\alpha = E_\beta$, where $E_\alpha = \{(x,y) : y \in F_2 \cdot_\alpha x\}$.

Determine whether the following hold:

(i) For every nonidentity element $x \in F_2$, there exists a free, p.m.p. action $\beta$ of $F_2$ on $(X,\mu)$ such that $E_\alpha = E_\beta$ and $x$ acts ergodically in $\beta$.

(ii) There exists a single free, p.m.p. action $\beta$ of $F_2$ on $(X,\mu)$ such that $E_\alpha = E_\beta$ and every nontrivial element of $F_2$ acts ergodically in $\beta$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory. Miller and Tserunyan have shown a strengthening of Hjorth's theorem on cost attained, producing free actions of $F_n$ in which each of the $n$ generators acts ergodically, but the question of obtaining a single orbit-equivalent action in which every nontrivial element of $F_2$ acts ergodically (and the per-element version (i)) does not appear to be resolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Nonamenable subforests of multi-ended quasi-pmp graphs (Chen, Tserunyan)
status_evidence.snippet: Their techniques give a significant strengthening of Hjorth's theorem: the action of F_n can be arranged so that each of the n generators alone acts ergodically.
status_evidence.claim: Miller–Tserunyan obtained orbit-equivalent free F_n actions in which each generator acts ergodically, but stronger ergodicity for all nontrivial elements is not established.

status_evidence.title: All properly ergodic Markov chains over a free group are orbit equivalent
status_evidence.snippet: All Bernoulli shifts over a free group are orbit equivalent; this is strengthened by replacing Bernoulli shifts by properly ergodic countable state Markov chains.
status_evidence.claim: Related orbit equivalence results for free group actions, but not addressing the precise problem.
